subtype: Approach: listening separately to each side first [Action]
passage:
Thursday. Sat with Minakshi first, half an hour in the small meeting room, and asked only two questions: what happened, and what do you need? Minakshi said Tarun kept rewriting the release script without telling anyone. Then Tarun, who said Minakshi had blocked his changes "for no reason" and that he just wanted to know what he owns. I said nothing about who was right. What I noticed: both described the same gap in different words. Nobody had ever said who owns the release task. Both of them looked relieved just to have been listened to. Tomorrow I'll draw up an ownership list and show it to each of them separately before we all meet.

Devika

qa.q: What two questions did Devika ask each colleague?
qa.a: Devika asked what happened and what do you need.

qa.q: How did Minakshi and Tarun seem to feel after being listened to?
qa.a: Both looked relieved, since each had been able to tell their side without being judged.

qa.q: What could Devika do next, and why?
qa.a: Devika could draft an ownership list and show it to each of them before they meet, because a clear owner for each task removes the gap the quarrel grew from.

qa.q: How might Tarun have felt about the release script being blocked?
qa.a: Tarun probably felt frustrated and unsure of the role, wanting to know what Tarun owns.

grounding: Illustrates a lead meeting two colleagues one at a time, asking what happened and what each needs, and finding the quarrel began over unclear ownership of a release task.

(Ira, the team lead, messages each of her two developers separately.)
Ira (to Eshaan): hey, got 15 min today? just you and me, no agenda except the release thing
Eshaan: sure. 3pm?
Ira (at 3:40): thanks for that. to check I got it: you thought the hotfix was yours to ship, and then Lina merged it without telling you
Eshaan: yes. I felt stupid in standup
Ira: and what do you need going forward?
Eshaan: just to know what's mine before Monday
Ira (to Lina): got time for a quick 1:1? want to hear your side of the release
Lina: ok, 5?
Ira (at 5:30): so you believed the hotfix was on you because the ticket had your name from last sprint
Lina: yes!! nobody said it moved
Ira: what would help?
Lina: a clear owner on each task. that's all 🙏
Ira (note to self): same problem, two names on one ticket. fix ownership, not people.

qa.q: What time did Ira meet Eshaan?
How did Eshaan feel after Lina merged the hotfix?
qa.a: Eshaan felt stupid and embarrassed in standup, because Lina merged the hotfix Eshaan expected to ship, without any warning.

qa.q: What else could Ira do now that she has heard both sides?
qa.a: She could write one clear owner on each release task and share it with both, so the ownership gap stops creating new fights.

qa.q: How might Lina see Ira's one-to-one meeting?
qa.a: Lina probably feels heard rather than accused, since Ira asked what happened and what would help instead of deciding who was wrong.

grounding: It shows a lead meeting two colleagues separately, asking what happened and what each needs, and discovering the fight came from unclear ownership of a release task.

passage:
The cooperative dairy office in Anand closed its shutter at six, but Chandrika asked Uday to stay back.
"Just tell me what happened at the collection counter yesterday. I'm not deciding anything yet."
Uday twisted his cap. "Nalini shouted at me in front of the farmers. She says I skipped the fat test on the evening batch. But nobody told me the evening batch was mine."
"And what do you need?"
"To know which batches I test. That's all."
The next morning, before the milk vans arrived, Chandrika sat with Nalini on the bench outside the chilling room.
"I checked the list on the wall," Nalini said. "It had Uday's name. Then Rameshbhai changed the shift, and the list still had it."
"What would help you?"
"A new list, and one person who signs it."
Chandrika wrote both answers in her ledger. The quarrel, she saw, was about an old list.

qa.q: Where did Chandrika sit with Nalini?
qa.a: She sat with Nalini on the bench outside the chilling room.

qa.q: What was Uday feeling as he twisted his cap?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and wronged, because Nalini had shouted at him in front of the farmers for a test he didn't know was his.

qa.q: What small step would help Chandrika most after these two talks?
qa.a: She could make a new signed testing list that shows which batches each person owns, so the old, outdated list stops causing blame.

qa.q: How does the separate talk look to Nalini?
qa.a: Nalini gets to explain the outdated list without Uday there, so she can feel heard rather than blamed and suggest a fix calmly.

grounding: It shows a lead hearing two colleagues one at a time, asking what happened and what each needs, and finding the fight began over unclear ownership of a task.
